subject: Close readiness playbook: TTFT & streaming latency benchmark
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.k@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@catalystlabs.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-30T09:00:00Z
Subject: Close readiness playbook: TTFT & streaming latency benchmark

Sarah / team —

Per our pre-close checklist, attaching a concise Mutual Action Plan (MAP) and the evaluation plan we intend to run this week so Catalyst Labs can sign off on performance ahead of procurement. High-level asks: confirm the acceptance thresholds below and sign the MAP spreadsheet by EOD Thursday so we can schedule the final dedicated run on Friday.

Key evaluation scope (short):
- Goal: Verify Time-to-First-Token (TTFT) and streaming tail latency under realistic chat workload; provide p50/p95/p99 for TTFT and per-token streaming latency.
- Models: redwood-1.3-stream-q4k (primary) and redwood-1.3-stream-q4k-fallback (quantized fallback).
- Sequence length: avg 256 tokens (max 1024), response window 512 tokens for long responses.
- Concurrency matrix: 1 / 8 / 32 / 128 concurrent users.
- Throughput targets: sustainable tokens/sec per GPU and aggregate throughput for dedicated pool (see MAP tab).
- Acceptance thresholds (proposed, please confirm):
  - TTFT p50 <= 40 ms, p95 <= 120 ms, p99 <= 240 ms
  - Streaming per-token latency p50 <= 5 ms, p95 <= 18 ms, p99 <= 40 ms at <=32 concurrency; expect some degradation at 128 concurrency but p99 <= 200 ms preferred
- Test harness: service-level workload generator (k6 + custom streamer), 5k-token warmup, three 10-minute steady-state windows per config.

Attachments: close_readiness_map.xlsx (MAP with milestones), test-harness-instructions.md (link inside spreadsheet).

Next steps requested from Catalyst:
1) Confirm acceptance thresholds or supply different values by 2027-05-30 17:00 PT.
2) Provide a procurement contact to circulate the MAP.

If agreed, our plan is to run the baseline (hosted) on Friday AM then the dedicated run Friday PM and deliver the bench report Saturday morning.

Thanks — Markus
Markus Klein
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: close_readiness_map.xlsx (Excel, 120KB)]

Thanks Markus — this looks thorough and aligned with our internal SLAs. A few quick notes:

- Procurement copied above (procurement@catalystlabs.com) will handle the MAP signature; they requested a one-week window for final legal redlines — is that compatible with your Friday run?
- Slight tweak to acceptance thresholds from our side: TTFT p95 <= 150 ms (we can relax p95 from 120 -> 150) and streaming p99 <= 60 ms at 32 concurrency. p99 at 128 we understand will be higher.
- Can you add a row in the MAP for maximum acceptable token-count per response (we typically cap at 600 tokens for UI considerations)?

If the team is okay with the small threshold adjustments and adds the token cap row, procurement will aim to sign the MAP next Tuesday; we still want the bench run this week for internal confidence.

-Sarah
Sarah Kim
Director of Product, Catalyst Labs

From: Markus Klein <markus.k@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@catalystlabs.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-31T08:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Close readiness playbook: TTFT & streaming latency benchmark — bench results attached

Sarah / team —

We ran the two-phase evaluation per the MAP this morning (hosted baseline) and this afternoon performed the dedicated-capacity run. Summary attached as bench_report_20270531.pdf; highlights below. Full logs and perf traces attached as perf_logs_20270531.zip.

Short summary (high level):
- Test config: redwood-1.3-stream-q4k, seq len 256 avg, warmup 5000 tokens, three 10-min windows per concurrency level.
- TTFT (ms) — hosted baseline / dedicated run (p50 / p95 / p99):
  - Concurrency 1: 34 / 92 / 170 (dedicated: 28 / 80 / 150)
  - Concurrency 8: 38 / 110 / 210 (dedicated: 30 / 95 / 180)
  - Concurrency 32: 45 / 140 / 320 (dedicated: 36 / 120 / 260)
  - Concurrency 128: 120 / 560 / 1200 (dedicated: 95 / 420 / 980)

- Streaming per-token latency (ms) median/p95/p99 at 32 concurrency (dedicated): 4.2 / 15.8 / 38.5
- Streaming per-token latency (ms) median/p95/p99 at 128 concurrency (dedicated): 9.6 / 60.2 / 185.4

Notes and interpretation:
- We met Sarah's relaxed p95 TTFT target (<=150ms) at <=32 concurrency on dedicated. p99 at 32 is above the original 240ms target (we measured 260ms dedicated) — close but slightly over.
- At 128 concurrency we see queuing behavior; p99 spikes in both hosted and dedicated. This is expected unless the customer uses larger dedicated pool sizing or request-level rate-limiting.
- Streaming per-token latency is within Catalyst's p99 <=60ms for 32 concurrency (we measured 38.5ms). At 128 concurrency the p99 increases but remains <200ms on dedicated.

Recommended close path:
1) Mark go for production if Catalyst accepts the TTFT p99 at 32 concurrency of <=260ms and agrees to a phased rollout with request-rate caps at 128 concurrency.
2) Offer a short burst policy (2x capacity for 10 minutes) for go-live day to smooth onboarding traffic.
3) Add an explicit note in the MAP that 128-concurrency sustained workloads should be under a dedicated larger pool configuration (we'll provide sizing guidance in MAP).

Attachments: bench_report_20270531.pdf (5 pages, charts + config), perf_logs_20270531.zip (raw traces).

I pasted the key result table into the attached PDF and into the MAP tab "BenchSummary" for quick reference. Let me know if you want a short walkthrough call this afternoon.

-Markus
